items.title: [13.x] Fix database cache lock aborting the transaction on PostgreSQL
CloudBootstrapper renumbers pgsql PDO options for -pooler hosts (array_merge on int keys)
items.body:
### Laravel Version

13.31.0 (same code on the current 13.x branch)

### PHP Version

8.4.25

### Database Driver & Version

pgsql, Laravel Cloud Serverless Postgres through the `-pooler` endpoint

### Description

When `database.connections.pgsql.host` contains `pg.laravel.cloud` and `-pooler`, `CloudBootstrapper::configureUnpooledPostgresConnection()` adds emulated prepares like this:

```php
$app['config']->set(
    'database.connections.pgsql.options',
    array_merge(
        $app['config']->get('database.connections.pgsql.options', []),
        [PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true],
    ),
);
```

PDO attribute keys are integers, and `array_merge()` renumbers integer keys. Any PDO options the app already set are therefore re-keyed from 0 and applied to the wrong attributes. For example:

```php
array_merge(
    [PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5, PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true, Pdo\Pgsql::ATTR_DISABLE_PREPARES => true],
    [PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true],
);
// [0 => 5, 1 => true, 2 => true, 3 => true]
// = ATTR_AUTOCOMMIT => 5, ATTR_PREFETCH => true, ATTR_TIMEOUT => 1, ATTR_ERRMODE => 1 (ERRMODE_WARNING)
```

Effects:

- `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES` itself is lost. So is any `ATTR_PERSISTENT` or `Pdo\Pgsql::ATTR_DISABLE_PREPARES` the app set.
- `ATTR_ERRMODE` becomes `ERRMODE_WARNING`. The key 3 value overrides the connector's default `ERRMODE_EXCEPTION`, so query errors surface as PHP warnings (`ErrorException`) instead of `QueryException`.
- The connect timeout becomes 1 second.

Because emulation is lost, pdo_pgsql uses named server-side prepared statements through the transaction pooler. With a libpq older than 17, pdo_pgsql frees statements with SQL `DEALLOCATE pdo_stmt_N`. PgBouncer (`max_prepared_statements` > 0) has renamed the statements to `PGBOUNCER_N`, so the `DEALLOCATE` fails with 26000. pdo_pgsql ignores that error, but the open transaction is aborted, and the next statement fails:

```
SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: ERROR: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block
```

We hit this in `DB::transaction()` blocks with more than one query (a deploy seeder) right after switching `DB_HOST` to the `-pooler` endpoint.

The default `config/database.php` sets no pgsql `options`, so apps on the stock config are not affected. Any app that sets PDO options on pgsql is.

### Steps To Reproduce

```php
config([
    'database.connections.pgsql.host' => 'ep-example-123456-pooler.us-east-2.pg.laravel.cloud',
    'database.connections.pgsql.options' => [
        PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5,
        PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true,
    ],
]);

\Illuminate\Foundation\CloudBootstrapper::configureUnpooledPostgresConnection(app());

var_dump(config('database.connections.pgsql.options'));
// array(3) { [0]=> int(5) [1]=> bool(true) [2]=> bool(true) }
// expected: [PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5, PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true, PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true]
```

End to end: a Laravel Cloud app whose pgsql connection sets any PDO options, `DB_HOST` pointed at the `-pooler` endpoint, and a `DB::transaction()` that runs two queries. It fails with 25P02 on the second query.

Suggested fix: assign the key instead of merging, for example `$app['config']->set('database.connections.pgsql.options.'.PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES, true)`, so existing integer keys are preserved and emulation is forced as intended.

items.title: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block on listener when implement ShoudlQueue
Database Lock fails on PostgreSQL if transaction in progress
items.body:
<!-- DO NOT THROW THIS AWAY -->
<!-- Fill out the FULL versions with patch versions -->

- Laravel Version: 8.27.0
- PHP Version: 7.4.15
- Database Driver & Version: PostgreSQL 13.2

### Description:
DatabaseLock.php raises unhandled QueryException inside catch.
` SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: 7 ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block (SQL: update "cache_locks" set "owner" = CWrOKyyPnGGBZbfG, "expiration" = 1613560215 where "key" = laravel_cachelaravel_unique_job:App\Jobs\UniqueJob123 and ("owner" = CWrOKyyPnGGBZbfG or "expiration" <= 1613473815))`

It seems that this can happen in a case where database lock is tried to acquire within transaction. I came across this since I have models which are saved with `->saveOrFail()` and after creation they trigger same job inside observers created method. That job is using `ShouldBeUnique` to ensure only one is in the end done.

Models successfully saved but these job creations are failing after first one is created.

### Steps To Reproduce:
This is simplest I could come up with. 

1. Setup Laravel with Postgresql
2. Setup database cache
3. Setup database cache_locks table
4. Setup database queues
4. Settings should be then in phpunit CACHE_DRIVER=database, QUEUE_CONNECTION=database
3. Create UniqueJob which implements `ShouldBeUnique`

Try to run test case:
```
public function test_example()
    {
        $this->getConnection()->beginTransaction();
        // On this call database.lock uses Insert and it works for the first time
        UniqueJob::dispatch();
        // On this call insert fails and it goes to catch but the update fails on the error
        UniqueJob::dispatch();
    }
```

I've also created project which reproduces this by running migrations and then running test TestJobs.php: 
https://github.com/fobin/laravel-unique-job

items.title: [10.x] Fix Postgres cache store failed to put exist cache in transaction
`Model::createOrFirst()` in Postgres transaction may trigger `SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: 7 ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block`
Missing error message when aborting a transaction (with postgres)
items.body:
<!-- DO NOT THROW THIS AWAY -->
<!-- Fill out the FULL versions with patch versions -->

- Laravel Version: 8.59.2 (Sail 1.8.4)
- PHP Version: 8.0.8
- Database Driver & Version: 
  - `sail php -r "echo(phpversion('pgsql'));"` -> 8.0.8
  - Postgres: 13.3-1.pgdg100+1

### Description:

When a transaction is aborted due exception the following PGSQL error message is written to the logs:

```
[2021-07-29 12:09:18] local.ERROR: SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: 7 ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block (SQL: select * from "trainings" where "trainings"."id" = 0a959b11-52a3-4f5f-b92b-0daf00e2bd4a limit 1) {"userId":"f013bd08-646f-45fe-bcdb-859fe00e27af","exception":"[object] (Illuminate\\Database\\QueryException(code: 25P02): SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: 7 ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block (SQL: select * from \"trainings\" where \"trainings\".\"id\" = 0a959b11-52a3-4f5f-b92b-0daf00e2bd4a limit 1) at /var/www/html/vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php:692)
[stacktrace]
#0 /var/www/html/vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php(652): Illuminate\\Database\\Connection->runQueryCallback()
#1 /var/www/html/vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php(360): Illuminate\\Database\\Connection->run()
#2 /var/www/html/vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Query/Builder.php(2351): Illuminate\\Database\\Connection->select()
// -- snip...
```

However this is not useful for debugging since it does not provide information about the error itself. It seems like while handling the original exception it does not get logged and is replaced by the `SQLSTATE[25P02]` exception, dropping the information about the original error. The only way to find out what went wrong is to follow the transaction step by step, wait for the exception to occur and then read the message with the debugger. The SQL statement within the error log is not the failing one, it was executed with the expected result and without error! The Exception message found with the debugger:

```
SQLSTATE[42P01]: Undefined table: 7 ERROR:  relation "appointment_module" does not exist
LINE 1: select * from "appointment_module" where "appointment_module...
                      ^ (SQL: select * from "appointment_module" where "appointment_module"."appointment_id" = 81e18055-fcb5-49ef-8829-bac8fa5d87e6)
```
*(I ran into this because I forgot to migrate ;P )*

In my opinion the original message should also be included/logged somehow for debugging reasons. That's why I consider this a bug though it is not stopping an error-free app from working properly.

*If I don't remember it wrong MySQL will include the error that failed the transaction into the transaction error message, making this less problematic but I'm not sure about this. Also I have not tested it for other RDBMS like Oracle/MSSQL.*

### Steps To Reproduce:

<!-- If possible, please provide a GitHub repository to demonstrate your issue -->
<!-- laravel new bug-report --github="--public" -->

1. Create new Laravel project and configure it for PGSQL
2. Create a transaction with `\DB::beginTRansaction();`
3. Execute a failing SQL statement like access to a non-existing table
4. Commit the transaction via `\DB::commit();`
5. Trigger execution
4. Try to determine the error that failed the transaction from the logs

items.title: Uncaught Predis exception Predis\Transaction\AbortedMultiExecException
items.body:
I am running the `queue:listen` command as a daemon and occasionally I get the following exceptions logged:

> Predis\Transaction\AbortedMultiExecException: The current transaction has been aborted by the server

This is thrown from the Predis library directly (var/www/010-windsordoc-api/vendor/predis/predis/lib/Predis/Client.php(402)) because the MultiExec call returns null. 

Can anyone explain why this is happening?
